rounds.method_summary: Phase 1 reproduction: official VAR-DD-d16 weights, single-step (t_list=0, loss_split_t=5) FID-50k evaluation per paper protocol. Measured FID 9.66 vs paper 9.94. bs reduced to 32 due to OOM at bs=64 (codebook nearest-neighbor memory spike). Establishes baseline anchor for Phase 2 optimization.

Diagnostic round: first end-to-end training pipeline verification with 10k teacher samples (cfg=1.5), 5k training steps, uniform time sampling, mse+ce loss. 2k-sample FID=240 (noisy, diagnostic only). Confirms training pipeline works end-to-end and produces diverse, non-collapsed outputs. Next: full 4h budget candidate with more teacher samples and more training steps.

rounds.method_summary: First full-budget candidate: 50k teacher samples (cfg=1.5, top_k=900, top_p=0.95), level-weighted time sampling (by token count per level), 28142 training steps in 2.7h, MSE+CE loss. FID-50k=163.53, far from baseline 9.66. Training loss plateaued at ~0.797. Self-implemented FM training pipeline verified to work end-to-end but quality is poor. Next: improve loss formulation and investigate token-level loss weighting to match DD paper approach more closely.

t0-importance time sampling (70% t=0) + level-balanced loss. Training interrupted at step 9200/30000 (~53min) with no checkpoint saved. Loss plateaued around 0.818 (mse≈0.020, ce≈8.0). Process killed during session interruption.

rounds.method_summary: Full-budget candidate with curriculum high-to-low time sampling (5-phase: high t -> t0 only). Teacher 50k cfg=1.5, 40000 steps in 151min, MSE+CE loss. FID-50k=167.92, worse than round3 163.53. Curriculum from scratch did not help; t=0 phase loss plateaued at 0.817 (CE ~8.0 barely below random 8.3). Next: warm start from official DD weights (v1.1) + t0_dominant + higher quality teacher samples.

Warm-start from official DD weights (v1.1) + t0_dominant time sampling (90% t=0) + cfg=3.0 teacher samples, lr=5e-5, ce_weight=0.3, 37k steps in 2.8h. FID-50k=166.83, essentially same as from-scratch (163-167). Key finding: full fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting - model completely overwrites official DD weights on small 50k dataset. Next: very low LR (5e-6) + t0_only + fewer steps for gentle fine-tuning without forgetting.

Round 7: two failed attempts. (1) warmstart_uniform_cfg3 ablation: started ~15:20, terminated by runner at 20:58:29 CST (launched after cutoff signal, per protocol). (2) warmstart_t0only_lowlr_cfg3 restart at 21:17: immediately failed with CLI error (unrecognized --save_interval). Hypothesis of very gentle fine-tuning (lr=1e-6, t0_only) not tested. Continued as round 8.

rounds.method_summary: Diagnostic round: very gentle fine-tuning (warmstart + t0_only + lr=1e-6 + 1000 steps + ce_weight=0.01). 10k cfg=3.0 teacher samples reused from round8 generation. FID-2k=28.29 vs baseline 28.11 (2k) — difference within noise, indicating gentle FT preserves most quality. Official 50k FID=9.66. Key finding: 2k FID has large upward bias (~28 vs ~9.7), so 2k results only usable for relative comparison. Next: test if more steps / different time sampling can improve vs baseline.

rounds.method_summary: Diagnostic round: warmstart + t0_importance (70% t=0) + MSE-only + 5000 steps + lr=2e-6 + 32k cfg=3.0 teacher. 5k-sample FID=62.63 (diagnostic only, score=null). Key finding: MSE-only training at moderate intensity causes severe quality degradation. Hypothesis: shared transformer backbone drifts to optimize MSE while untrained logits head degrades, hurting coarse-level predictions (used in inference via get_final_sequence with split_t=5). Next: test MSE+CE balanced loss to confirm hypothesis.

rounds.method_summary: Diagnostic round: warmstart + t0_only + MSE+CE (ce_weight=0.3) + 5000 steps + lr=2e-6 + 32k cfg=3.0 teacher. 2k-sample FID=50.79 (diagnostic only, score=null). Key finding: MSE+CE preserves quality much better than MSE-only (estimated 2k FID 50.8 vs ~71 for MSE-only at same intensity), confirming logits head drift hypothesis. However, even with MSE+CE, 5k steps at lr=2e-6 causes severe degradation (50.8 vs baseline 28.1 at 2k). Overfitting to 32k samples is the primary bottleneck. Next: test higher-quality teacher samples (cfg=5.0) with very gentle fine-tuning to see if quality can improve over baseline.

rounds.method_summary: Full candidate: warm-start from official DD + t0_only + MSE+CE (ce_weight=0.3) + 1000 steps + lr=1e-6 + 50k cfg=5.0 teacher samples. FID-50k=9.78 vs baseline 9.66. Very close to baseline (+0.12, within noise margin). Key finding: very gentle fine-tuning on cfg=5.0 teacher samples largely preserves baseline quality. The cfg=5.0 teacher did not improve FID beyond baseline. Model barely changed with 1k steps at lr=1e-6. Retained as best trained candidate.

Full candidate: warm-start from official DD + t0_only + MSE+CE (ce_weight=0.3) + 600 steps + lr=5e-7 + 50k cfg=7.0 teacher samples. FID-50k=9.77 vs baseline 9.66 and R12 9.78. Ultra-gentle fine-tuning (fewer steps, lower LR than R12) with higher-CFG teacher (cfg=7.0 vs cfg=5.0). Marginal improvement over R12 (+0.01, within noise). Neither beats baseline. Key finding: increasing teacher CFG from 5.0 to 7.0 with ultra-gentle FT does not meaningfully improve FID beyond baseline. Overfitting to 50k samples and the shared backbone/logits-head coupling remain the fundamental bottlenecks preventing improvement from warm-start fine-tuning.

dd-selfproto-v1.3; actual current independent CLI research. Hard-example proposal selection (max LPIPS disagreement per class group) paired with early-scale-biased time sampling (power law t=U^2.5). 256 samples x 4 proposals = 1024 generated, 256 selected. Uniform weighting. First evaluation attempt failed with INFRASTRUCTURE_RUNTIME error; recovered by trusted backend reusing original frozen checkpoint to regenerate all 50000 samples and compute independent FID. No retraining, no re-submission — this is evaluation recovery of the same method, not an additional method round.

dd-selfproto-v1.3; actual current independent CLI research. Easy-example proposal selection (min LPIPS disagreement per class group) paired with uniform time sampling. 256 samples x 4 proposals = 1024 generated, 256 selected. Uniform weighting. Joint two-factor flip vs round-01 (max-LPIPS + early-bias). Improves on round-01 by 0.34 FID but still 0.12 worse than no-training baseline at 256 samples.
